query: Clacton by-election August 2026 Nigel Farage candidates contesting - which parties standing aside, who is running against him, full candidate list
answer:
I've completed the research on the Clacton by-election. Here's a summary of what I found:

**The Clacton by-election (13 August 2026)** was triggered by Nigel Farage's resignation as MP (announced 7 July, effective 8 July 2026) amid a parliamentary standards investigation into his finances. Farage is re-contesting the seat.

**Parties standing aside (5):** Labour, Conservatives, Liberal Democrats, Greens, and Restore Britain — all boycotting, characterizing it as a "circus"/"fake by-election"/"vanity project" and calling for the standards investigation to conclude first. This leaves **no major-party opponent**, with novelty candidate **Count Binface** described as the "main challenger."

**Candidate field:** Between 14 and 18 candidates were declared as of nomination week (nominations close today, 17 July). Notable candidates running against Farage include Count Binface, Laurence Fox (Reclaim), Kai Stephens (British Democratic Party), Adham Alkhatip (Forward Party), John Stevens (Rejoin EU), Piers Corbyn, and multiple Monster Raving Loony Party and Independent candidates.

**Key caveat:** The official list is only confirmed once the Statement of Persons Nominated is published after nominations close — the field was still evolving at the time of research.

The full structured findings, including the complete candidate list, party rationales, timeline, and all sources, have been submitted via the StructuredOutput tool.

key_facts: Clacton by-election polling day is Thursday 13 August 2026, triggered by Nigel Farage's resignation as MP (announced 7 July 2026, effective 8 July 2026).

Farage resigned amid a parliamentary standards investigation into his finances (alleged undeclared £5m gift from Christopher Harborne and donations linked to George Cottrell) and is re-contesting the seat.
Five parties are standing aside/boycotting: Labour, Conservatives, Liberal Democrats, Greens, and Restore Britain — leaving no major-party opponent.
Novelty candidate Count Binface is widely described as the 'main challenger' to Farage given the major-party boycott.
Labour called it 'a circus'; Kemi Badenoch (Conservatives) called it a 'fake by-election'; Ed Davey (Lib Dems) called it Farage's 'vanity project.'
Between 14 (PollCheck) and 18 (Democracy Club) candidates were declared as of nomination week; official list confirmed via Statement of Persons Nominated after nominations close 17 July 2026 at 4pm.

Declared candidates include Nigel Farage (Reform UK), Count Binface, Laurence Fox (Reclaim Party), Kai Stephens (British Democratic Party), Adham Alkhatip (Forward Party), John Stevens (Rejoin EU), Piers Corbyn (Ind), and multiple Independents and Monster Raving Loony Party candidates.
Three candidates withdrew: Rob Pownall (Independent fox-costume campaigner), Amelia Randall (Balanced Britain Party), and a Climate Party candidate.
Nomination timetable: writ approved 9 July, Notice of Election 13 July, nominations 14–17 July 2026, administered by Tendring District Council.
